standfirst: The fish nervous necrosis viruses. Four proteins on two segments, and the headline fact is a negative one: unlike the insect nodaviruses, the betanodavirus capsid is not cleaved. Its RNA2 ORF “carries the catalytic D-75 residue but lacks the site for autocatalytic proteolysis” (PMID 9672600), so no beta and no gamma are declared here.

modules.Betanodavirus: The largest module of the four, 1,456 genomes. RNA1 carries protein A plus B1 and B2 from subgenomic RNA3; RNA2 carries one uncleaved coat protein of 338–340 aa. Every length window comes from the literature, because this genus is dominated by partial typing deposits — the median coat protein record is 181 aa against a true 338, and the median polymerase record is 300 against 982.

gaps: Beta and gamma are probed for and come back ABSENT, which is the required result rather than a shortfall: it proves the alphanodavirus cleavage rule did not leak across into a genus that does not use it. protein C and protein D are single deposits using positional letters that name no homology group, and are left to the homology rescue.
derived: No mature peptides are declared in this module. The N-ARM, S domain and P domain described in the capsid structure (PMID 26491970) are regions of one continuous chain, not products, and modelling them would assert a cleavage the literature explicitly rules out.

why.B1: Real, and its start codon has never been published. PMID 19136133 cloned the RGNNV B1 gene as 336 nt and showed the protein is an anti-necrotic death factor, but no paper gives a start coordinate and no RefSeq annotates a B1 CDS anywhere in the genus — BV-BRC holds 2 deposits across 1,456 genomes. The 115 members here were extracted from the genomes under the one property the literature does fix: B1 is in frame with protein A and shares its stop, so an accepted member must be an exact C-terminal substring of protein A from its own genome. 124 of 124 passed.
